I work high-acuity crisis lines for Protocall Services (988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline network partner serving New Mexico) and am completing an M.S. in clinical psychology at New Mexico Highlands University, with a thesis on outdoor mindfulness-based behavioral activation for depression.

## What I Do

**Crisis work.** Crisis counselor with Protocall Services (988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline network partner serving New Mexico). High-acuity phone and chat triage and intervention, using ACT and behavioral activation. Friday–Monday nights.

**Research.** M.S. in clinical psychology at New Mexico Highlands University. Thesis: (outdoor) mindfulness-based behavioral activation for depression. Longitudinal design, psychometrics, psychological assessment, EEG. R for data work.

**Building & writing.** This site — a Quarto artifact, hand-set in an academic brutalist design and deployed as static files — plus research tooling in R, Python, Quarto, Markdown, LaTeX, and Git, and science communication. Before clinical work: journalism as a city reporter, copyeditor, and culture writer.

## Background

**Clinical training** — Crisis intervention, ACT, behavioral activation. Graduate training in psychometrics, psychological assessment, and longitudinal research methods at New Mexico Highlands University.

**Journalism** — City reporting, copyediting, culture writing. Local politics, food, arts. Accuracy on a deadline.

**St. John's College** — B.A., philosophy (Great Books program). Close reading, Socratic dialogue, ancient Greek (reading).

## Also True

- **Zazen:** Sōtō Zen, personal practice — student, not teacher
- **Spinoza:** ethics, philosophy of mind; the undergraduate focus that stuck
- **Systems thinking:** class, power, institutional critique

## Current Status

- **Thesis:** data collection and analysis complete; manuscript in progress
- **Location:** Albuquerque, New Mexico
- **Open to:** behavioral-health research, mental-health technology, clinical data, and science communication roles
